brief.headline: Two full sessions have now passed without an official exchange board being published, so the headline price on this page is Thursday's - and the week that starts today carries two central-bank decisions that matter more to this metal than anything on its own supply side.
bullets: WHAT MOVED - NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. No metal traded over the weekend, and the exchange has still not published Friday's official board. The last published settlement remains Thursday's 1.46% rally to $3,303 per tonne, the best level since mid-August, on warehouse stock at a thirty-six-year low. The only newer public mark is an independent price reference showing the metal handing back 0.81% on Friday to close at $3,292.50 after a very large upside surprise in US employment. That reference has not moved since. Every exchange figure on this page is Thursday's and is labelled as Thursday's.

WHY IT MATTERS THAT THE BOARD IS LATE. A missing official is normally a housekeeping problem. It is more than that here because the market is sitting on an unresolved contradiction - a thirty-six-year inventory low alongside a front-month curve that refuses to pay anything for prompt metal - and the settlement that would either confirm or break that pattern is the one that has not appeared. Until it does, the most reliable reading of Friday comes from the independent reference and from the macro that drove it, not from the exchange.

THE WEEK AHEAD IS A MACRO WEEK, NOT A METALS WEEK. The European Central Bank decides on Thursday 10-September with a quarter-point rise fully priced after euro-area August inflation rebounded to 3.3%, the highest since September 2023. The US Federal Reserve follows on Wednesday 16-September, and after August payrolls printed roughly three times consensus, traders are pricing the possibility of a rise rather than a cut. Two major central banks tightening inside a week is a direct headwind for a dollar-priced industrial metal and it raises the discount rate on every curtailed smelter that is weighing a restart.

WHAT TO WATCH, IN ORDER. First, whether Friday's official appears today and whether it confirms the give-back the independent reference already shows; when it does, the board, the fifteen-session windows and the weekly history row should all advance together. Second, the two central-bank decisions. Third, the Asian quarterly premium negotiation, where sellers have opened roughly a fifth below the record and buyers are pushing lower still - the clearest available statement of what people who actually move metal believe about physical tightness, and it currently disagrees with the inventory headline.

lme.commentary: THE LAST PUBLISHED OFFICIAL IS 03-SEPTEMBER: CASH $3,303.00, THREE-MONTH $3,303.50, STOCK 245,975 TONNES. THE 04-SEPTEMBER OFFICIAL HAS NOT BEEN PUBLISHED ON ANY OF FIVE WESTMETALL PAGES CHECKED THIS MORNING, so the chart, the board and the fifteen-session windows all stop at Thursday and nothing has been extrapolated onto Friday. THE 03-SEPTEMBER SESSION WAS GENUINELY STRONG: cash rose 1.46%, cleared $3,300 for the first time since 12-August, and led the entire LME board when copper cash managed +0.03%, nickel +0.51%, zinc -0.11% and lead -0.16%. WHAT HAPPENED NEXT IS KNOWN FROM AN INDEPENDENT PUBLISHER AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY: Trading Economics recorded aluminium at $3,292.65 on 04-September, down 0.81%, after an intraday high near $3,310 that was an over-three-week peak. US August payrolls printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, traders moved toward pricing a Federal Reserve hike, and the dollar index rose 0.27%. THE PATTERN IS A FAILED BREAKOUT AT THE LEVEL THE BULLISH TECHNICAL COUNT NEEDED TO CLEAR. THE CURVE REMAINS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THIS PANEL AND IT HAS NOT CHANGED ITS MIND: cash sits $0.50 BELOW three-month - a CONTANGO on the convention used throughout this page - and the single-session backwardation of 02-September reversed within twenty-four hours. A thirty-six-year inventory low that cannot generate a bid front end is the central fact of this market, and the inventory series has now stopped arguing with the curve: exchange stock has drawn just 950 tonnes across eight published sessions.

regional.basis: S&P GLOBAL PLATTS SETTLED THE Q3-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM AT A RECORD $395/t CIF JAPAN, ASSESSED 06-JULY-2026, UP 12.4% ON Q2-2026's $351.50/t. THIS IS A CONTRACTED QUARTERLY BENCHMARK, NOT A DAILY PRICE, AND IT IS CARRIED AT ITS SETTLEMENT VALUE UNTIL Q4 RESOLVES - it is not stale, it is simply the number that governs the quarter. THE FORWARD PICTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE HEADLINE AND IT IS PUBLIC: Reuters reported on 02-September, citing four sources involved in the talks, that producers including Rio Tinto and South32 have offered $310-$325/t for October-December, down 18-22%, with Japanese buyers targeting below $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes.

SPOT CIF JAPAN IS A PERIODIC ASSESSMENT CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK OF $370/t AND NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC ASSESSMENT WAS RETRIEVABLE THIS MORNING. THE STALENESS IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN DISGUISED, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LIMITATION ON THIS PANEL FOR A PHYSICAL READER. WHAT THE SPOT-VERSUS-CONTRACT GAP IMPLIES IS WORTH STATING: a $370 spot against a $395 contracted quarterly settlement means the quarter was contracted above where the market has since been clearing, which is exactly the condition that produces a large downward reset at the next negotiation - and the published Q4 producer offers of $310-325 are consistent with that arithmetic rather than a surprise against it.

EUROPEAN DUTY-UNPAID IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED ASSESSMENT OF $485/t AND NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK WAS RETRIEVABLE. THE EUROPEAN LEG HAS BECOME AN EXPLICIT INPUT INTO THE ASIAN BENCHMARK AND THAT IS THE REASON TO WATCH IT: the published rationale for the lower Q4 Japanese offers cites softer premiums in Europe alongside a positive progress report on Middle East production. EUROPE IS ALSO WHERE THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE LANDS - the EU import ban on Russian primary aluminium takes effect 31-December-2026, and this is the premium that must absorb it. A soft duty-unpaid premium three months ahead of a ban on a major supply source is a genuine puzzle worth holding in mind.

ROTTERDAM BILLET DUTY-PAID IS CARRIED AT $1,212.50/t, ITS LAST PUBLISHED ASSESSMENT, WITH NO NEWER DATED PUBLIC MARK RETRIEVABLE. BILLET PREMIUM IS THE CLEANEST AVAILABLE READ ON EUROPEAN EXTRUSION DEMAND BECAUSE IT IS PAID BY FABRICATORS RATHER THAN TRADERS, AND IT SITS WELL ABOVE ITS PRIOR-PERIOD AVERAGE OF $1,144. THE DEMAND BACKDROP BEHIND IT DETERIORATED THIS WEEK: Volkswagen's management board confirmed on 05-September that it will close four German plants by 2034 - Emden and Zwickau in 2031, Hanover in 2032, Neckarsulm in 2034 - and guided full-year 2026 group sales down to approximately 8.5 million units. That is a dated, disclosed, structural reduction in European automotive aluminium demand, and while the plant closures are years out the volume guidance is now.

THE US MIDWEST TRANSACTION PRICE IS CARRIED AT $2,094/t, ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK, DOWN SHARPLY FROM THE $2,380 PRIOR AND FROM A PRIOR-PERIOD AVERAGE OF $2,561.90. THIS ROW IS TARIFF-INFLATED AND THAT IS THE ONLY WAY TO READ IT HONESTLY: with Section 232 at 50% on articles, the statutory tariff leg alone on a $3,303.00 cash price is approximately $1,651.50, which is roughly 79% of the entire quoted premium. THE REMAINING FIFTH IS THE ACTUAL PHYSICAL MARKET. A reader who treats this number as a demand signal will misread it completely; it is primarily a tax, and it mechanically rises whenever the metal price rises even if physical conditions are unchanged.

THE DUTY-PAID US MIDWEST ROW MATCHES THE TRANSACTION ROW AT $2,094/t BY CONSTRUCTION AND IS CARRIED AT THE SAME LAST PUBLISHED MARK. THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS REFRESHED EVERY RUN EVEN WHEN THE ASSESSMENT IS NOT, BECAUSE THE TARIFF LEG IS A CALCULATION ON THE VERIFIED RATE AND THE CURRENT CASH PRICE RATHER THAN AN ASSESSMENT: 50% of $3,303.00 is $1,651.50. THE RATE ITSELF IS RE-VERIFIED EACH RUN AND REMAINS 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, WITH ANNEX I-C CARVE-OUTS AT 15% FOR JAPAN, KOREA, THE UNITED KINGDOM, SWITZERLAND, TAIWAN AND THE EUROPEAN UNION. A reported US-Canada reduction to 25% has been discussed publicly but is NOT law and is not reflected here.

drivers.text: Q4-2026 producer offers are public and 18-22% below the Q3 record — Reuters reported on 02-September-2026, citing four sources involved in the quarterly talks, that top global producers including Rio Tinto and South32 offered Japanese buyers $310-$325 per tonne for October-December shipments, down 18% to 22% on the Q3 settlement of $395. Japanese buyers are targeting below $300. The stated rationale is a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer premiums in Europe. Talks began the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later in September, so the range on this page should tighten before it resolves.
drivers.source: Reuters via MINING.COM, 02-Sep-2026 - producers offer Japanese buyers lower Q4 premiums

drivers.text: The inventory argument behind a high premium weakened materially this week — The strongest case for defending a record premium was that physical metal was disappearing. Two independent public series stopped supporting that in the same week. LME exchange stock drew only 250 tonnes on its latest published session to 245,975 t, and across the eight most recent published sessions it has fallen just 950 tonnes in total. SMM reported on 05-September that Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory across eight major markets was 681,000 tonnes, down only 2,000 tonnes on the week and essentially unchanged from the end of August, though still 62,000 tonnes below the same week of 2025. Two inventory series flattening simultaneously during peak restocking season is a weaker premium argument than either was a month ago.
drivers.source: SMM via AL Circle, 05-Sep-2026 - China aluminium ingot social inventory 681,000 t, down 2,000 t on the week

drivers.text: The US premium is roughly 79% statutory tariff and the metal rally made that worse — With Section 232 at 50% on articles and a verified LME cash price of $3,303.00, the tariff leg alone is approximately $1,651.50 per tonne against a quoted US Midwest duty-paid premium of $2,094 - about 79% of the whole number. The arithmetic is mechanical: because the tariff is levied ad valorem, every dollar the metal price rises inflates the quoted US premium without any change in physical conditions. Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% apply to Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU; a reported US-Canada reduction to 25% has been discussed but is not law.
drivers.source: Sandler Travis & Rosenberg - Section 232 tariff actions resource page (rate verification)

drivers.text: Demand-side news this week was uniformly negative in both major consuming regions — Premiums are paid by physical consumers, so end-market data matters more to them than exchange inventory. Three dated public releases landed on 05-September and all three point the same way. The China Passenger Car Association put August retail passenger-vehicle sales at 1.626 million units, down 19% year on year, with new-energy retail at 1.069 million units, down 4% year on year. Volkswagen confirmed it will close four German plants by 2034 and guided full-year 2026 group sales down to approximately 8.5 million units. Eurostat put euro-area August inflation at 3.3%, the highest since September 2023, with a 25 basis point ECB hike fully priced for next week. Weaker automotive demand and tighter European policy are both premium-negative.
drivers.source: SMM - China August passenger car sales down 19% YoY; Volkswagen plant closures; Eurozone August CPI 3.3% (all published 05-Sep-2026)

alumina.notes: ALUMINA REMAINS THE ONE PART OF THE VALUE CHAIN IN GENUINE SURPLUS AND THAT IS WHY SMELTER MARGINS HAVE BEEN WIDE ALL YEAR. NO NEW PUBLIC ASSESSMENT PRINTED INTO THIS WEEKEND WINDOW, SO EVERY ROW ON THIS PANEL IS CARRIED AT ITS LAST DATED MARK WITH THE DATE SHOWN, AND NOTHING IS INTERPOLATED. SMM's market commentary continues to describe the Chinese alumina market as one of STRONG SUPPLY AND WEAK DEMAND that limits rebound room, which is consistent with the refinery-side surplus this page has been reporting. THE SINGLE LARGEST IDENTIFIABLE RISK TO THAT SURPLUS IS ALUNORTE, THE LARGEST REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA. It cut production to 50% of capacity during August in a natural-gas supply dispute and has since ramped back to full capacity following a TEMPORARY TERMINAL ACCESS AGREEMENT with its gas supplier. The word temporary is the whole risk: the restoration is conditional on an expiring arrangement rather than on a resolved dispute, and the same disruption previously drove Norsk Hydro to declare force majeure on aluminium sales. A RENEWED ALUNORTE INTERRUPTION WOULD COMPRESS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT MARGIN DRIVER IN THE INDUSTRY, WHICH MAKES IT THE MOST UNDER-WEIGHTED RISK ON THIS PAGE. The reason it is under-weighted is that alumina surplus is a quiet, structural, boring fact while the metal-side inventory headline is dramatic - and this week demonstrated that the dramatic fact was the less reliable one.

CTP SETTLES ON A MONTHLY CYCLE ALONGSIDE PREBAKED ANODES, TYPICALLY AROUND THE 17TH-18TH, so a genuine new point is due in the coming fortnight rather than this weekend. WHY THIS ROW MATTERS DESPITE ITS SMALL CONSUMPTION RATIO: pitch is roughly a tenth of a tonne per tonne of aluminium but it is the binder without which anodes cannot be made, its supply is tied to metallurgical coke output rather than to aluminium demand, and it has risen approximately 5.4% since late July on the published weekly marks. It is a small line that moves for reasons entirely outside this industry's control.

Contracts are bilateral, confidential, jurisdiction-specific and often decades long, so any chart drawn here would be an invention rather than a measurement. THE ROW IS CARRIED AS A RANGE WITH THE CONSUMPTION RATIO SHOWN BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT CAN HONESTLY BE PUBLISHED. WHAT IS PUBLIC AND DATED IS THE STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE, AND IT IS ABUNDANT: roughly 50% of EU primary capacity has been curtailed since 2022 on power costs; Slovalco's restart of a first 75,000 tonnes required an agreement with the Slovak government; Alcoa secured Portland power to mid-2035 before committing; and Rio Tinto's Tomago is underpinned by a government support package and a ten-year power purchase agreement running to 2038. EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS A DISCLOSED TRANSACTION IN WHICH POWER, NOT METAL PRICE, WAS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT.

items.label: Aluminium fluoride (AlF3)
items.note: NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN - THE FIRST NUMERIC POINT ADDED TO THIS ROW SINCE 16-AUGUST. SMM's fluoride-salt weekly review, published 05-September-2026 and carried by AL Circle, puts mainstream SMM quotations for aluminium fluoride at RMB 11,500-12,000 per tonne, up from the RMB 11,200-11,800 range carried previously. THE POINT APPENDED IS 11,500 BECAUSE THIS ROW'S HIST SERIES IS CONSISTENTLY BUILT ON THE LOW END OF THE SMM MAINSTREAM RANGE - the 16-August point of 11,200 was the low end of 11,200-11,800 - and changing basis mid-series would corrupt the sparkline. THE DRIVERS ARE DISCLOSED AND SPECIFIC. Benchmark downstream enterprises finalised September tender prices during the week and raised them by RMB 300-500 per tonne overall, with the high-grade transaction centre climbing to RMB 12,000-12,500 per tonne. The cost push is upstream fluorspar: 97% fluorite wet powder is at RMB 3,350-3,850 per tonne delivered and holding firm at high levels, because high-pressure mine safety inspections have continued unabated - Inner Mongolia's 'Double Ten Measures' inspections, Zhejiang's small-mine closure policy, and ongoing compliance checks in Jiangxi and Fujian have delayed production resumptions and kept fluorite inventory low. Anhydrous hydrogen fluoride September long-term contracts were raised above RMB 15,000 per tonne. Partly offsetting, aluminium hydroxide was flat week on week at an SMM weighted average of RMB 1,650 per tonne and sulphuric acid eased. SMM'S OWN SUMMARY OF THE MARKET IS 'COST SUPPORT, TIGHT SUPPLY, AND INELASTIC DEMAND', with producers running at low operating loads on narrow margins and prioritising long-term contract delivery. THE READ-ACROSS FOR A SMELTER IS THAT THIS IS A COST INCREASE DRIVEN ENTIRELY BY CHINESE MINE-SAFETY ENFORCEMENT UPSTREAM - it will not respond to aluminium demand and it will not ease until fluorspar supply is released.

items.label: Cryolite / bath makeup
items.note: NEW PUBLIC MARK APPENDED THIS RUN. The same SMM fluoride-salt weekly review of 05-September-2026 reports that cryolite spot prices FIRMED, with SMM quotations at RMB 8,000-9,000 per tonne against the RMB 7,500-9,000 carried previously. THE POINT APPENDED IS 8,000, THE LOW END OF THE SMM RANGE, WHICH IS THE SAME BASIS AS EVERY PRIOR POINT IN THIS SERIES - the 16-August point of 7,500 was the low end of 7,500-9,000. THE TREND FLAG IS CUT FROM FLAT TO UP: this series sat at RMB 7,000 from May through late June, moved to 7,500 in August and is now at 8,000, which is a 14.3% increase from the spring plateau and the first genuinely sustained move in the row. THE CAUSE IS THE SAME AS THE ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE ROW AND THAT IS THE POINT WORTH DRAWING OUT: both are fluorine chemistry, both depend on fluorspar, and Chinese mine-safety enforcement is now visibly repricing the entire bath-chemistry basket at once rather than one line at a time. Consumption is small at roughly 10 kg per tonne of metal, so the absolute margin impact is modest, but two correlated bath inputs moving together is a cleaner signal about upstream fluorspar than either one alone.

items.label: Cathode / graphite blocks
items.note: NO NEW PUBLIC MARK PRINTED FOR THIS ROW IN THE 06-SEPTEMBER WINDOW, so the value and the hist series are carried unchanged and no point has been appended. Gaps are left as gaps; nothing on this row is interpolated or estimated between published marks. NO PUBLIC PRICE SERIES EXISTS FOR THIS LINE AND HIST THEREFORE STAYS EMPTY BY DESIGN. Cathode and graphite block supply is contracted bilaterally, usually as part of a relining package rather than as a traded commodity, and no independent index publishes a transacted price. THE ROW IS RETAINED BECAUSE THE COST IS REAL AND LUMPY EVEN THOUGH IT CANNOT BE CHARTED: a pot reline is a capital event with a multi-year cycle, and the relevant commercial question is scheduling and availability rather than a spot price. Publishing an invented series here would be worse than publishing nothing.

items.note: NO NEW PUBLIC MARK PRINTED FOR THIS ROW IN THE 06-SEPTEMBER WINDOW, so the value and the hist series are carried unchanged and no point has been appended. Gaps are left as gaps; nothing on this row is interpolated or estimated between published marks. NO NEW POINT THIS RUN. THE TRAJECTORY IS THE STORY AND IT IS STEEP: 8,650 on 10-July, 9,100 on 17-July, 9,050 on 06-August, 9,350 on 20-August, 9,400 on 25-August - an 8.7% increase across seven weeks on the published marks. SILICON IS THE PRINCIPAL ALLOYING ELEMENT FOR CASTING AND AUTOMOTIVE ALLOYS, so this line bears directly on value-added product cost rather than on primary metal cost, and it is rising into a Chinese vehicle market that has just reported an August retail decline of 19% year on year. Rising input cost into falling downstream demand is the least comfortable combination on this panel.

items.label: Magnesium (99.9%)

MAGNESIUM IS THE QUIETEST ROW ON THIS PANEL AND THAT IS INFORMATIVE IN ITSELF: it sits below its June level of RMB 16,300 and has simply stopped moving, while every fluorine-chemistry line beside it is rising. A stable magnesium price alongside rising fluoride salts and rising silicon tells you the cost pressure in this basket is specific to particular upstream supply constraints rather than being a broad Chinese industrial-input inflation.

items.label: Copper (LME)
items.note: LME official CASH settlement, on the same uniform board as the LME Board table - THE 03-SEPTEMBER-2026 OFFICIAL. The per-metal ENGLISH copper daily table was checked directly this morning and it too ends at 03-September, which is one of five independent confirmations that the publication gap is at the source rather than in this page's retrieval. THE SERIES THEREFORE STILL RUNS 13-AUGUST TO 03-SEPTEMBER AND ENDS ON THE BOARD'S OWN SESSION, WHICH IS THE CONSISTENCY REQUIREMENT FOR THIS ROW. WHY COPPER SITS IN A SMELTER INPUT BASKET AT ALL: it is the busbar, cable and conductor metal in the potroom and the substation, so it is a real capital and maintenance input, and it is also the best available high-frequency read on industrial risk appetite. WHAT IT SAYS TODAY IS THAT A GENUINE SQUEEZE IS UNWINDING - cash $14,359.00 over a $14,275.00 three-month is an $84.00 backwardation, down from more than $500 on 17-August per Reuters, on a second consecutive stock build to 234,650 t. That is the clearest available counter-example to the idea that low exchange inventory automatically means a bid front end.

CONSUMPTION IS ONE TO TWO KILOGRAMMES PER TONNE, SO THE COST IMPACT IS TRIVIAL AND THE AVAILABILITY IMPACT IS NOT: without grain refiner the casthouse cannot make saleable billet to specification, which makes this a supply-security line rather than a cost line. It is retained for completeness and flagged honestly as unpriceable in public.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THE ROW IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND THE RISK INTENSIFIED THIS WEEK. Trading Economics reported that the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities has raised uncertainty over the potential return of aluminium supplies from the Persian Gulf. THE PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES REMAIN VISIBLE ACROSS THREE SEPARATE PRODUCERS - EGA at 315 of 1,262 cells with its refinery at roughly 50%, Qatalum curtailed at roughly 60% of a 648,000-tonne nameplate on reduced gas, and Alba with reduction lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March. THE TENSION WORTH NAMING IS THAT PRODUCERS CITED A POSITIVE MIDDLE EAST PROGRESS REPORT WHEN CUTTING Q4 JAPANESE PREMIUM OFFERS 18-22%: the disruption is real and the market's willingness to pay for it is falling at the same time.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: RE-STATED THIS RUN ON A CURRENT PUBLIC BASIS RATHER THAN CARRIED. Traffic through Bab el Mandeb is down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and the US Maritime Administration advisory 2026-006 covering the Red Sea, Bab el Mandeb, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea and Somali Basin REMAINS IN FORCE THROUGH 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Suez transits remain far below pre-crisis normal and carriers are still routing via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe voyages. THE DIRECTION FLAG IS DOWN BECAUSE THE CORRIDOR IS DEGRADED, NOT BECAUSE COSTS ARE FALLING - the two Middle East chokepoints on this page are now both impaired simultaneously, Hormuz by live hostilities and Bab el Mandeb by a blockade with a dated advisory attached, and a producer routing Gulf or Red Sea metal to Europe has no unimpaired option. Sources: https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks ; https://gcaptain.com/suez-canal-traffic-stalls-at-60-below-normal-despite-100-days-without-houthi-attacks/

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: STILL NO PUBLIC REPRICE, AND THE ABSENCE IS NOW OLD ENOUGH TO BE A FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. The last public mark this page can cite is 7.5-10% of hull value from 22-July, against a 1-3% pre-conflict norm. Since that mark, at least four merchant vessels have been reported struck in or near the Strait, including two on Monday night and further attacks reported on 01/02-September. HULL-VALUE PREMIUM IS THE FIRST THING THAT REPRICES AFTER TANKERS ARE PHYSICALLY HIT, so the 22-July figure should be treated as a FLOOR and explicitly not as a current quote. This page will not estimate the current level because war-risk rates are negotiated bilaterally and no public assessment exists. THE COMMERCIAL POINT STANDS WITHOUT THE NUMBER: war-risk cost sits inside every regional premium on this page simultaneously and is completely invisible in the LME flat price, which is one reason a falling LME and firm premiums are not the contradiction they appear to be.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK WITH THE STALENESS DISCLOSED; DRY-BULK INDICES DO NOT PUBLISH AT THE WEEKEND AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED. THE BDI MATTERS TO THIS INDUSTRY PRINCIPALLY THROUGH BAUXITE AND ALUMINA RATHER THAN THROUGH METAL, because the upstream legs of the chain are the bulk-freight legs: roughly two tonnes of alumina and four to five tonnes of bauxite move for every tonne of metal produced. A freight move is therefore an upstream cost event with a lag, not a metal-price event.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: CARRIED AT ITS LAST PUBLISHED MARK AND THE ASSESSMENT DATE IS SHOWN. CONTAINER FREIGHT IS THE WRONG INDEX FOR PRIMARY METAL AND IS RETAINED FOR THE DOWNSTREAM LEG: extrusions, rolled coil, finished components and value-added products move in boxes rather than in bulk. IT IS THEREFORE THE FREIGHT LINE THAT BEARS ON THE FABRICATED-PRODUCT PREMIUMS ON THIS PAGE - Rotterdam billets, Southeast Asian billet premiums - rather than on the LME price.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: GENERIC COMMERCIAL NOTE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN - BUT WITH A NEW FORWARD-LOOKING POINT WORTH FLAGGING GENERICALLY. Contracts written across the Gulf disruption commonly carry force-majeure, war-risk cost-pass-through and demurrage clauses that were drafted for a CLOSED strait. A partial, temporary, 30-to-60-day corridor arrangement of the kind announced on 26-August sits awkwardly between 'closed' and 'open' and is exactly the situation in which such clauses become contested rather than automatic. Anyone with live tonnage under those terms should expect the interpretation question to arrive before the logistics question resolves. This is a general market observation about contract structure and carries no company-specific or confidential content.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: BRENT CLOSED THE WEEK AT $96.28 ON 04-SEPTEMBER, UP 0.80% ON THE DAY, AND TRADING ECONOMICS FLAGGED IT AS THE STRONGEST WEEKLY GAIN IN SOME TIME; WTI was $91.48, up 0.20%. ENERGY IS THE LARGEST SINGLE COST LINE IN A SMELTER AND THE MOST IMPORTANT MACRO ROW ON THIS PAGE FOR A COST READER. The rise is consistent with the Strait of Hormuz situation remaining unresolved rather than with demand strength, which is the uncomfortable combination for the industry: the same disruption that supports the metal price also raises the cost of producing it and of shipping it. A firm crude tape alongside a hawkish employment print is also mildly stagflationary in character, and that is the macro backdrop the 16-September Federal Reserve decision now sits against.

row.label: European gas TTF
row.note: TTF WAS EUR 71.96/MWh ON 04-SEPTEMBER, UP 0.20% ON THE DAY. EUROPEAN GAS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON EUROPEAN SMELTER RESTART ECONOMICS AND THE REASON ROUGHLY HALF OF EU PRIMARY CAPACITY HAS SAT CURTAILED SINCE 2022. THE LEVEL MATTERS MORE THAN THE DAILY MOVE HERE AND IT IS STILL HIGH ENOUGH TO KEEP MOST RESTART DECISIONS MARGINAL - which is precisely why the Slovalco restart is being executed with a government agreement behind it rather than on merchant power alone, and why Alcoa needed a secured power arrangement at Portland to mid-2035 before committing. GAS IS ALSO THE DIRECT LINK TO THE ALUMINA SIDE: the Alunorte cut to 50% of capacity in August was a gas-supply dispute, not a market event, and it is running on a temporary terminal-access agreement.

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: THE DOLLAR INDEX ROSE 0.27% TO 99.176 ON 04-SEPTEMBER AND THAT MOVE IS THE CLEANEST SINGLE EXPLANATION FOR ALUMINIUM'S 0.81% GIVE-BACK ON THE SAME DAY. THE CAUSE IS DATED AND PUBLIC: US non-farm payrolls for August printed +162,000 against a consensus near 53,000, June was revised up 11,000 and July up 44,000 for a combined +55,000, unemployment held at 4.1%, average hourly earnings rose 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year, and participation rose from 61.4% to 61.6%. TRADERS RAISED BETS ON A FEDERAL RESERVE HIKE AT THE 16-SEPTEMBER MEETING. THIS RESOLVES A DISAGREEMENT THIS PAGE HAS BEEN CARRYING FOR SEVERAL RUNS between a Reuters read that September hike expectations were FADING and an SMM read that they had HEATED UP. THE DATA CAME DOWN ON THE HAWKISH SIDE. For a dollar-denominated metal that is a direct headwind, and it removes the currency tailwind that was worth roughly a fifth of the 03-September rally.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD WAS 1.16143 ON 04-SEPTEMBER, DOWN 0.10% ON THE DAY, HAVING RISEN 0.31% ON THE PRIOR OFFICIAL SESSION TO AN LME FIXING OF 1.16140. THE EURO LEG NOW HAS ITS OWN CATALYST AND IT POINTS THE OTHER WAY FROM THE DOLLAR LEG. Eurostat preliminary data published 05-September put euro-area August CPI at 3.3% year on year, the highest since September 2023, with core CPI at 2.4% easing slightly from 2.5% in July; the market has FULLY PRICED A 25 BASIS POINT EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK HIKE NEXT WEEK and anticipates further increases thereafter. TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS BOTH LEANING HAWKISH IN THE SAME WEEK IS AN UNAMBIGUOUS HEADWIND FOR INDUSTRIAL METALS DEMAND, and it is a materially different regime from the one this page was describing a fortnight ago.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: USD/CNY WAS 6.70783 ON 04-SEPTEMBER, DOWN 0.15% - A MARGINALLY STRONGER YUAN AGAINST A STRONGER DOLLAR, WHICH IS UNUSUAL AND WORTH NOTING. A firmer yuan makes dollar-priced imports slightly cheaper for Chinese buyers and marginally raises the dollar value of Chinese exports. THE CHINESE DEMAND SIGNAL THIS WEEK IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE AND IT IS NEGATIVE: the China Passenger Car Association's preliminary August figures, published 05-September, put retail passenger-vehicle sales at 1.626 million units, DOWN 19% YEAR ON YEAR though up 11% on the month, with new-energy retail at 1.069 million units, down 4% year on year. Automotive is one of the three largest end-uses for primary aluminium, and a 19% annual decline in the world's largest vehicle market sits awkwardly beside a Chinese ingot inventory series that has just stopped drawing.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: THE US TEN-YEAR WAS 4.789% AFTER THE PAYROLL PRINT. THE LEVEL IS THE STORY RATHER THAN THE DAILY CHANGE: a ten-year approaching 4.8% alongside a labour market strong enough to revive hike talk is a high-cost-of-capital environment, and that bears directly on the two things this page tracks on the supply side. FIRST, RESTART AND EXPANSION ECONOMICS: every curtailed smelter restart, every new greenfield project and every refinery debottleneck is a long-dated capital decision discounted at these rates, and higher rates push marginal projects out rather than in. SECOND, INVENTORY FINANCING: carrying metal costs money, and a flat curve plus a high funding rate is precisely the combination that discourages anyone from holding stock on warrant. THAT IS A CREDIBLE, MUNDANE AND OFTEN OVERLOOKED EXPLANATION FOR WHY EXCHANGE INVENTORY CAN SIT AT A THIRTY-SIX-YEAR LOW WITHOUT THE CURVE EVER BACKWARDATING - the metal has moved off-warrant because financing it on-warrant does not pay.

headlines.title: THE 04-SEPTEMBER LME OFFICIAL BOARD REMAINS UNPUBLISHED AS OF MONDAY 07-SEPTEMBER, A SECOND BUSINESS DAY, AND WAS RE-VERIFIED THIS MORNING ACROSS FOUR SOURCE PAGES - THE ENGLISH AND GERMAN OVERVIEWS, EACH REQUESTED WITH A CACHE-BUSTING QUERY STRING, AND THE PER-METAL ENGLISH ALUMINIUM AND COPPER DAILY TABLES - ALL OF WHICH STILL END AT 03-SEPTEMBER. The English and German boards agree line for line across all six metals, all six warehouse lines and all three EUR/USD fixings, which rules out a stale cache on one language version and establishes this as a publication gap at the source. Friday's session traded and settled; only its official publication is missing. Nothing traded over the weekend, so no newer public mark of any kind exists and the independent price reference is also unchanged at its Friday close of $3,292.50. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THAT EVERY EXCHANGE FIGURE ON THIS PAGE IS THURSDAY'S: cash, three-month, the spread, all six warehouse lines, the three EUR/USD fixings, the fifteen-session base-metal windows, the copper input row and the weekly price-history row are all held rather than rolled, and none of them has been estimated. Today's own official prints at 13:20 London, after this compile, so on the current pattern the source could be two sessions behind by this evening. THIS IS A DATA-AVAILABILITY ITEM RATHER THAN A MARKET EVENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS TAGGED MIXED - it changes what can be said with confidence, not what the metal is worth.

US AUGUST NON-FARM PAYROLLS PRINTED +162,000 AGAINST A CONSENSUS NEAR 53,000, A THREEFOLD UPSIDE SURPRISE, AND TRADERS RAISED BETS ON A FEDERAL RESERVE HIKE AT THE 16-SEPTEMBER MEETING. June was revised up 11,000 and July up 44,000, making the two months combined 55,000 higher than previously reported. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%, average hourly earnings rose 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year, the average workweek edged up to 34.4 hours and participation rose from 61.4% to 61.6%. Leisure and hospitality led with 62,000 jobs added. THIS RESOLVES A DISAGREEMENT THIS PAGE HAS CARRIED FOR SEVERAL RUNS between a Reuters read that September hike expectations were fading and an SMM read that they had heated up - the data came down firmly on the hawkish side. The dollar index rose 0.27% to 99.176 and aluminium fell 0.81% on the Trading Economics reference to $3,292.65 after an intraday high near $3,310.

EURO-AREA AUGUST INFLATION REBOUNDED TO 3.3% YEAR ON YEAR ON PRELIMINARY EUROSTAT DATA, THE HIGHEST SINCE SEPTEMBER 2023, AND THE MARKET HAS FULLY PRICED A 25 BASIS POINT EUROPEAN CENTRAL BANK HIKE NEXT WEEK WITH FURTHER INCREASES ANTICIPATED THEREAFTER. Core CPI was 2.4%, easing slightly from 2.5% in July. TWO MAJOR CENTRAL BANKS LEANING HAWKISH IN THE SAME WEEK IS AN UNAMBIGUOUS HEADWIND FOR INDUSTRIAL METALS and it is a materially different macro regime from the one this page was describing a fortnight ago, when the live question was the timing of cuts. For a European smelter the second-order effect is worse than the first: higher policy rates raise the discount rate on every curtailed-capacity restart decision in a region where roughly half of primary capacity has been offline since 2022.

CHINA'S AUGUST RETAIL PASSENGER-VEHICLE SALES FELL 19% YEAR ON YEAR TO 1.626 MILLION UNITS ON PRELIMINARY CHINA PASSENGER CAR ASSOCIATION FIGURES, THOUGH THEY ROSE 11% ON THE MONTH. New-energy retail was 1.069 million units, DOWN 4% YEAR ON YEAR and up 12% on the month. AUTOMOTIVE IS ONE OF THE THREE LARGEST END-USES FOR PRIMARY ALUMINIUM AND A 19% ANNUAL DECLINE IN THE WORLD'S LARGEST VEHICLE MARKET IS NOT A ROUNDING ERROR. The month-on-month gain is the seasonal peak arriving on schedule; the year-on-year collapse is the underlying trend. Read alongside a Chinese ingot social-inventory series that drew only 2,000 tonnes in the same week, the seasonal restock looks weaker than the calendar would normally deliver. BYD was the standout on the other side, delivering over 440,000 units, up nearly 18% year on year, so the weakness is in the aggregate rather than uniform across makers.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORY ACROSS THE EIGHT MAJOR MARKETS WAS 681,000 TONNES ON 05-SEPTEMBER, DOWN ONLY 2,000 TONNES ON THE WEEK AND ESSENTIALLY UNCHANGED FROM THE END OF AUGUST, PER SMM. Regional moves were minimal: Wuxi and Hangzhou each added 1,000 tonnes while Foshan drew 1,000 tonnes. The series remains 62,000 tonnes below the same week of 2025, so the year-on-year comparison is still constructive. THE WEEK-ON-WEEK NUMBER IS THE ONE THAT CHANGED AND IT MATTERS BECAUSE THIS PAGE HAS BEEN CITING A LONG RUN OF CONSECUTIVE CHINESE DRAWS AS A PILLAR OF THE TIGHTNESS CASE. A 2,000-tonne draw during what should be peak September restocking is a stall, not a drawdown. It arrives in the same week that the LME series drew just 250 tonnes, which means both major public inventory series flattened simultaneously.

THE LME CASH OFFICIAL CLIMBED 1.46% TO $3,303.00 ON 03-SEPTEMBER WITH STOCKS AT 245,975 TONNES, CLEARING $3,300 FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 12-AUGUST AND LEADING THE ENTIRE LME BOARD - copper cash was +0.03%, nickel +0.51%, zinc -0.11% and lead -0.16%. THIS REMAINS THE MOST RECENT PUBLISHED OFFICIAL. Five separate Westmetall pages were checked on 06-September - the English overview, the English overview with a cache-busting query, the German overview with its own cache-busting query, and the per-metal English aluminium and copper daily tables - and all five end at 03-September, so the 04-September official has not been published anywhere reachable. TOP GLOBAL PRODUCERS INCLUDING RIO TINTO AND SOUTH32 HAVE OFFERED JAPANESE BUYERS $310-$325 PER TONNE FOR OCTOBER-DECEMBER SHIPMENTS, DOWN 18% TO 22% ON THE RECORD Q3 SETTLEMENT OF $395, ACCORDING TO REUTERS CITING FOUR SOURCES INVOLVED IN THE TALKS. Japanese buyers are targeting below $300 as Asian balances ease on rising Indonesian volumes; the stated producer rationale is a positive progress report on Middle East production and softer premiums in Europe. Talks began in the week of 24-August and are expected to run through later in September. THE SIGNIFICANCE IS THAT THE PEOPLE WHO SELL THE METAL ARE OPENING A FIFTH BELOW THE RECORD IN THE SAME FORTNIGHT THAT EXCHANGE STOCK PRINTED A THIRTY-SIX-YEAR LOW. That remains the single best argument on this page for treating the exchange inventory headline with care.

VOLKSWAGEN'S MANAGEMENT BOARD HAS DECIDED TO SHUT PRODUCTION AT FOUR GERMAN PLANTS - EMDEN AND ZWICKAU CEASING IN 2031, HANOVER IN 2032 AND NECKARSULM IN 2034 - AND THE GROUP EXPECTS FULL-YEAR 2026 GLOBAL SALES OF APPROXIMATELY 8.5 MILLION UNITS. THE PLANT CLOSURES ARE YEARS OUT BUT THE VOLUME GUIDANCE IS NOW, AND BOTH BEAR ON EUROPEAN ALUMINIUM DEMAND. Automotive is a principal end-market for rolled sheet, extruded structural components and casting alloys, and Germany is the largest single European consumer of all three. For the billet and rolled-product premiums tracked on this page this is a structural rather than cyclical signal, and it lands in the same week that European inflation rebounded to 3.3% and a central bank hike was fully priced.

SEPTEMBER ALUMINIUM FLUORIDE TENDER PRICES WERE RAISED BY RMB 300-500 PER TONNE AND SMM MAINSTREAM QUOTATIONS NOW STAND AT RMB 11,500-12,000 PER TONNE, WITH THE HIGH-GRADE TRANSACTION CENTRE AT RMB 12,000-12,500; CRYOLITE FIRMED TO RMB 8,000-9,000 PER TONNE. THE DRIVER IS UPSTREAM FLUORSPAR AND IT IS A REGULATORY SUPPLY SHOCK RATHER THAN A DEMAND PULL: 97% fluorite wet powder is holding at RMB 3,350-3,850 per tonne delivered because high-pressure mine safety inspections have continued unabated, with Inner Mongolia's 'Double Ten Measures', Zhejiang's small-mine closure policy and ongoing compliance checks in Jiangxi and Fujian delaying production resumptions and keeping inventory low. Anhydrous hydrogen fluoride September long-term contracts were raised above RMB 15,000 per tonne. SMM characterises the market as cost support, tight supply and inelastic demand. Both bath-chemistry lines on this page's input basket have been marked up as a result - the first new numeric points on either row since 16-August.

SLOVALCO IS RESTARTING THE FIRST 75,000 TONNES OF A TOTAL 175,000 TONNES OF ANNUAL CAPACITY AFTER THREE YEARS OFFLINE, WITH PRODUCTION EXPECTED TO START DURING THE FOURTH QUARTER OF 2026, ENABLED BY AN AGREEMENT WITH THE SLOVAK GOVERNMENT. Capacity was curtailed in 2022 on high power prices, and roughly 50% of EU primary capacity has been offline since. SEPARATELY, MAGNITUDE 7 METALS HAS RESTARTED ITS MISSOURI SMELTER, ADDING 75,000 TONNES OF ANNUAL PRIMARY PRODUCTION BY THE END OF 2026, AND ALCOA'S Q2 ALUMINIUM PRODUCTION ROSE 5% QUARTER ON QUARTER TO 636,000 TONNES ON THE RESTORED PORTLAND CAPACITY. THE RESTART PIPELINE IS THE PRINCIPAL MEDIUM-TERM COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE INVENTORY HEADLINE and it is now visible in three separate disclosed transactions rather than in forecasts. Note that each required a power solution first - a government agreement, a secured PPA, or both.

THE US DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE HAS BACKED A $4 BILLION OKLAHOMA ALUMINIUM SMELTER PROJECT AS THE LEGAL DEBATE AROUND IT INTENSIFIES, ACCORDING TO PUBLIC REPORTING THIS WEEK. GREENFIELD PRIMARY CAPACITY IN THE UNITED STATES HAS BEEN EFFECTIVELY ABSENT FOR DECADES, SO ANY CREDIBLE PROJECT IS STRUCTURALLY SIGNIFICANT EVEN IF IT IS YEARS FROM METAL. The commercial logic is straightforward and it is created by policy rather than by the market: with Section 232 at 50% on articles, domestic production enjoys a statutory advantage worth roughly $1,650 per tonne at current prices, which is precisely the kind of protection that makes an otherwise marginal high-power-cost jurisdiction financeable. It is also why the US Midwest premium should be read as a tax rather than as a demand signal.

THE ALUNORTE REFINERY IN BRAZIL, THE LARGEST OUTSIDE CHINA, TEMPORARILY CUT PRODUCTION TO 50% OF CAPACITY IN AUGUST ON A NATURAL-GAS SUPPLY DISPUTE AND HAS SINCE RAMPED BACK TO FULL CAPACITY FOLLOWING A TEMPORARY TERMINAL ACCESS AGREEMENT WITH ITS GAS SUPPLIER. THE WORD TEMPORARY IS THE ENTIRE RISK. This page corrected the Alunorte status in the previous run and the correction stands, but the restoration is conditional on an expiring arrangement rather than on a resolved dispute. ALUMINA IS THE ONE PART OF THE CHAIN IN GENUINE SURPLUS - SMM describes the Chinese market as strong supply and weak demand, limiting rebound room - and that surplus is what has been widening smelter margins all year. A renewed Alunorte interruption would compress the single most important margin driver in the industry, which makes this the most under-weighted risk on the page.

ZINC HOLDS A $127.50 BACKWARDATION THAT WIDENED ON A SESSION WHEN 9,975 TONNES WERE DELIVERED INTO LME WAREHOUSES - A 9.9% SINGLE-SESSION INVENTORY BUILD THAT FAILED TO CLOSE THE CURVE - AND THE EXCHANGE DISCLOSES THAT ONE ENTITY HOLDS MORE THAN 50% OF ZINC WARRANTS AND CASH CONTRACTS. COPPER'S BACKWARDATION MEANWHILE COMPRESSED TO $84.00 FROM MORE THAN $500 ON 17-AUGUST AS AVAILABLE STOCKS EDGED HIGHER, WITH A SECOND CONSECUTIVE WAREHOUSE BUILD TO 234,650 TONNES. THE PAIR IS THE MOST USEFUL COMPARISON AVAILABLE FOR AN ALUMINIUM READER. Zinc shows what a genuinely controlled front end looks like; copper shows a real squeeze unwinding. Aluminium's $0.50 contango on a thirty-six-year inventory low resembles neither, which is the strongest available evidence that low registered stock is not by itself creating prompt scarcity.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXPORTS ROSE 18.7% YEAR ON YEAR IN JULY AS PRODUCERS SHIPPED METAL DESPITE BEIJING'S 45 MILLION TONNE OUTPUT CAP, WITH MUTED DOMESTIC DEMAND FREEING VOLUME FOR EXPORT AND PARTLY EASING THE SHORTAGES CREATED BY THE MIDDLE EAST DISRUPTION. CHINESE OPERATORS REMAIN AT OR THROUGH THE POLICY CEILING WITH OUTPUT STABLE, MARGINS WIDE AND EXPORTS ELEVATED. THE COMBINATION MATTERS MORE THAN ANY SINGLE COMPONENT: a capped output ceiling is structurally bullish, but wide margins plus a shrinking domestic vehicle market plus elevated exports is a configuration that pushes metal out of China into precisely the regions where premiums have been highest. That is the mechanism by which the Asian premium benchmark is being reset 18-22% lower for the fourth quarter.

THE LATEST ESCALATION IN US-IRAN HOSTILITIES HAS RAISED UNCERTAINTY OVER THE POTENTIAL RETURN OF ALUMINIUM SUPPLIES FROM THE PERSIAN GULF, AND THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ REMAINS SEVERELY IMPAIRED. EGA'S AL TAWEELAH IS ON A PARTIAL RESTART WITH 315 OF 1,262 CELLS RUNNING AND THE REFINERY AT ROUGHLY 50%, WITH PRE-WAR OUTPUT REAFFIRMED ONLY FOR Q1-2027; QATALUM REMAINS CURTAILED AT ROUGHLY 60% OF ITS 648,000-TONNE NAMEPLATE ON REDUCED GAS WITH A SECOND HYDRO FORCE MAJEURE OUTSTANDING; AND ALBA'S REDUCTION LINES 1, 2 AND 3 HAVE BEEN IDLED SINCE MARCH, ACCOUNTING FOR 19% OF ITS 1,623,000 TONNES OF CAPACITY WITH NO RESTART ANNOUNCED. THIS IS THE LARGEST SINGLE BULLISH FACT ON THE PAGE AND IT IS ALSO THE MOST GENUINELY UNCERTAIN. Brent closed the week at $96.28, up 0.80%, on its strongest weekly gain in some time - which supports the metal price and simultaneously raises the cost of producing and shipping it.

SECTION 232 REMAINS VERIFIED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, WITH ANNEX I-C CARVE-OUTS AT 15% FOR JAPAN, KOREA, THE UNITED KINGDOM, SWITZERLAND, TAIWAN AND THE EUROPEAN UNION; THE EU DUTY ON THIRD-COUNTRY PRIMARY METAL REMAINS 6%. A REPORTED US-CANADA REDUCTION TO 25% HAS BEEN DISCUSSED PUBLICLY BUT IS NOT LAW AND IS NOT REFLECTED IN ANY NUMBER ON THIS PAGE. THE RATE IS RE-VERIFIED EVERY RUN BECAUSE THE ENTIRE US PREMIUM DEPENDS ON IT: at a $3,303.00 cash price the tariff leg alone is approximately $1,651.50, roughly 79% of the quoted $2,094 duty-paid premium. THE LARGEST SCHEDULED TRADE EVENT REMAINS THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKING EFFECT 31-DECEMBER-2026, which must be absorbed by a European duty-unpaid premium currently assessed at only $485 per tonne.

THE SECONDARY ALUMINUM COALITION FOR AMERICA IS PUBLICLY ARGUING THAT RECYCLED METAL CAN CLOSE THE US SUPPLY GAP FASTER AND AT LOWER COST THAN NEW PRIMARY CAPACITY. THE ARGUMENT DESERVES SERIOUS WEIGHT ON A PAGE THAT SPENDS MOST OF ITS ATTENTION ON PRIMARY SMELTERS. Secondary production requires roughly 5% of the energy of primary, can be built in a fraction of the time, and does not need a decade-long power purchase agreement - which is exactly the constraint that has blocked every primary restart discussed on this page. If the US supply response to Section 232 arrives predominantly through recycling rather than through new pots, the medium-term primary deficit narrows less than the greenfield announcements imply, and the value-added end of the market changes shape faster than the primary end.

SHFE ALUMINIUM EDGED UP WITH THE REBOUND PACE SLOWING, WHILE THE ALUMINA MARKET SHOWS STRONG SUPPLY AND WEAK DEMAND THAT LIMITS ITS REBOUND ROOM, PER SMM'S MARKET COMMENTARY. SEPARATELY SMM HAS DESCRIBED ACCELERATED DESTOCKING OF ALUMINIUM INGOTS DURING THE PEAK SEASON AS SUPPORTING PRICES IN THE SHORT TERM - AND THAT FRAMING NOW SITS AWKWARDLY BESIDE THE ACTUAL 05-SEPTEMBER INVENTORY PRINT OF A 2,000-TONNE WEEKLY DRAW TO 681,000 TONNES. This page shows the tension rather than resolving it by preference: the commentary describes an accelerating destock, the measured series shows a stall, and the measured series is the harder evidence. AUGUST BILLET PREMIUMS IN SOUTHEAST ASIA WERE BROADLY STEADY WITH VIETNAM EDGING SLIGHTLY LOWER, which is consistent with the softer regional balance that producers cited when opening the Q4 Japanese talks 18-22% below the record.

Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

status.name: US / Canada trade policy (Section 232)
status.status: 50% ON ARTICLES, 25% ON DERIVATIVES - VERIFIED; A US-CANADA CUT TO 25% IS REPORTED BUT NOT LAW
status.impact: Mixed (the largest single swing factor in the US delivered premium)
status.update: RE-CHECKED 07-SEPTEMBER AND CARRIED UNCHANGED - NO NEW DATED COMPANY DISCLOSURE OR PRESS ITEM PRINTED OVER THE WEEKEND. RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE PRIMARY SOURCE THIS RUN AND UNCHANGED. Proclamation 11032 of 01-June-2026, published at 91 FR 34085, sets 50% on aluminium articles and Annex I-A derivatives and 25% on Annex I-B derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. A REPORTED US-CANADA REDUCTION TO 25% HAS BEEN DISCUSSED PUBLICLY BUT IS NOT LAW AND IS NOT REFLECTED IN ANY NUMBER ON THIS PAGE. THE ARITHMETIC MOVED TODAY EVEN THOUGH THE POLICY DID NOT, and the mechanism is worth stating because it is counterintuitive: the duty is ad valorem, so at a $3,303.00 cash settlement the pure tariff component of the US delivered premium is 0.50 x $3,303.00 = $1,651.50/t, up $23.75 on the session purely because the metal rallied. Against a fixed assessed premium of $2,094 that leaves an implied market component of about $442.50, DOWN from $466.25 - so a 1.46% metal rally mechanically made the US premium look 5.1% less market-driven without one physical fact changing in the United States. THE COMPARISON THAT SIZES THE DISTORTION: US duty-paid at $2,094 is 4.3x European duty-unpaid at $485 and 5.3x the Japanese Q3 contract at $395 on the same metal at the same moment. Strip the $1,651.50 statutory wedge and the residual sits between the two.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY. THEY ARE RE-RATED THIS RUN, AND THE TRIGGER IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN A CALENDAR DATE: the Strait of Hormuz de-escalation that this page carried from 26-August - an Iran-Oman announcement of a planned safe maritime corridor - BROKE DOWN OVER THE WEEKEND. US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, adjacent to the Strait, on Sunday 30-AUGUST; Iran retaliated against US bases; and the IRGC has claimed that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait. Reporting on 31-August describes the renewed hostilities as having dashed hopes of near-term normalisation of transit, and Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it while the LME was closed. THE COUNTER-SIGNAL IS GIVEN EQUAL WEIGHT AND IS EQUALLY DATED: on 01-September President Trump stated that strikes against Iran would be LIMITED and that the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large volumes of oil moving out, while Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed expanded secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners and attributed the Iranian action to sanctions pressure. THE TWO READS ARE NOT RECONCILED HERE BECAUSE THE MARKET HAS NOT RECONCILED THEM EITHER, and no LME session has yet had the opportunity to express a view. SECOND STRUCTURAL POINT, UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE BUT NOW SIMULTANEOUS WITH THE FIRST: Bab el Mandeb transits are down roughly 24% since the Houthi maritime blockade imposed on Saudi Arabia in July 2026, and US MARAD advisory 2026-006 remains in force through 22-SEPTEMBER-2026. Both Middle East chokepoints are impaired at the same time, which leaves a Gulf or Red Sea shipper with no unimpaired routing to Europe and is the physical reason freight is inflating faster than any other cost on this page. THIRD, THE SANCTIONS CLOCK: the LME has required attestations to warrant Russian aluminium in EU-listed warehouses since 25-February-2026, and the EU import ban on Russian aluminium takes effect 31-DECEMBER-2026 - a dated, certain change to the availability of the metal that dominates LME warrantable stock.
